summary.text: A 59-year-old woman presented with right eye pain and vision loss after being struck by a support post while working in the fields. She had had bilateral trabeculectomy with 0.04% MMC for bilateral POAG five years earlier. The right eye had a scleral flap defect with choroidal prolapse into the subconjunctival space, aqueous humor leakage, loss of the anterior chamber and choroidal detachment, with visual acuity logMAR 0.7 and IOP 3 mmHg.

Two days of rest, eye drops and oral acetazolamide failed to improve the leakage and anterior chamber depth, so repair surgery was performed. The bleb was incised at the base of the fornix, preserved sclera was trimmed and sutured with 10-0 nylon over the choroidal herniation, and the conjunctiva was rotated forward and sutured. Betamethasone and moxifloxacin drops were given from postoperative day 1, and a dorzolamide/timolol drop was added on day 3 for elevated IOP.

After the adjustment the IOP decreased to approximately 15 mmHg. The anterior chamber depth remained normal postoperatively and no aqueous humor leakage was observed. The abstract reports good IOP and no complications. At two-year follow-up the right eye had IOP 12 mmHg and corrected logMAR visual acuity 1.2 on dorzolamide/timolol eye drops.

summary.text: A 76-year-old male consulted a nearby hospital for decreased visual acuity in the right eye and was referred. He had had bilateral supratemporal trabeculectomy with 0.04% MMC for POAG three years earlier and a right eye filtering bleb infection two years earlier, managed with anterior chamber irrigation, intravitreal antibiotic injection and conjunctival resection at another hospital.

The right eye had poor corrected logMAR visual acuity 0.4, IOP 4 mmHg, aqueous humor leakage from an avascular filtering bleb, scleral flap melting and choroidal detachment, with the anterior chamber depth maintained and the intraocular lens stable. Surgical management was chosen: the bleb was incised, a preserved scleral patch was sutured over the defect, and the avascular conjunctiva was excised and advanced.

Postoperatively the leakage and choroidal detachment disappeared and betamethasone and gatifloxacin were given. The next day IOP was 44 mmHg and acetazolamide, latanoprost and dorzolamide/timolol were started; it fell to 27 mmHg two days after surgery and 12 mmHg on the third day, then rose again to 20 mmHg on the sixth day and did not decrease.

An Ahmed Glaucoma Valve was inserted on postoperative day 24 with its main body fixed inferotemporally and the tube tip in the ciliary sulcus. Postoperatively the IOP remained stable at about 12 mmHg over one year with an eye drop. The authors state that the damaged area improved with successful anatomical repair, and that the elevated IOP was managed with the valve.
